metrics.title: Curvature-ranked, occupancy-weighted top-10 emission hit rate of the level-1 cell partition, measured over chance.
metrics.formula: N = 24587 items, K = 256 codes, L levels. c1(i) in {1..K} is the level-1 code of item i. G_c = {i : c1(i) = c}, n_c = |G_c|, m = #{c : n_c > 0}. kappa < 0 is the frozen reference's curvature (kappa = -1 if the reference does not state one); beta = sqrt(|kappa|). p_i = exp_0^kappa(s_i) = tanh(beta |s_i| / 2) * s_i / (beta |s_i|), with s_i the frozen reference source representation of item i and exp_0^kappa(0) = 0. d_kappa(x,y) = (1/beta) * arcosh(1 + 2|kappa| |x-y|^2 / ((1-|kappa||x|^2)(1-|kappa||y|^2))). bar(S) is the Klein-Einstein hyperbolic midpoint of the set S: k_i = 2 p_i / (1 + |kappa||p_i|^2), gamma_i = 1/sqrt(1 - |kappa||k_i|^2), kbar = sum_i gamma_i k_i / sum_i gamma_i, bar(S) = kbar / (1 + sqrt(1 - |kappa||kbar|^2)). b_c = bar(G_c), computed once per occupied cell. For each training example e = (H_e, t_e) with H_e the history item ids and t_e the target item id: q_e = bar({p_i : i in H_e}); rank the m occupied cells by d_kappa(q_e, b_c) ascending, ties broken by ascending code index c; let S_e = sum of n_{c'} over all cells c' ranked strictly ahead of c1(t_e); hit_e = min(1, max(0, (10 - S_e) / n_{c1(t_e)})). RESULT = (mean_e hit_e - 10/N) / (1 - 10/N). One scalar; higher is better.
metrics.inputs: the exported SID table (integer code per item for levels 1..L, N rows and the item-id order); the frozen Issue #126 reference source-representation matrix s_i (N x d, learned on training pairs only) together with its curvature kappa; and the TRAINING split as (history item ids, target item id) pairs. Nothing else: no recall values, no Stage-3 output, no validation or test interaction.
metrics.geometry: the construction is a Poincare-ball computation of fixed negative curvature. Curvature enters in three places: the exponential map at the origin that places each reference vector in B_kappa; the conformal factor (1 - |kappa||x|^2) inside the geodesic distance, which inflates distance near the ball boundary, so a cell whose centre sits at radius 0.9 is ranked as the hyperbolic distance demands and not as its chord suggests; and the Lorentz factors gamma_i that weight the Klein-Einstein barycentre of a cell and of a history. The cell ranking that produces hit_e is a geodesic ranking around a geodesic barycentre; kappa is taken from the reference and never fitted, and no other constant appears.
metrics.why: it is an estimator of Recall@10 itself, not a proxy for tightness. Model Stage 3 as ordering items by the hyperbolic proximity of their level-1 cell centre to the history barycentre, and as being uniform inside a cell because the level-1 code is all it knows. Under that model hit_e is exactly the probability that the target is among the 10 emitted items, and 10/N is the exact chance level for any table under a target-independent ranking. Consequences: a one-code table has S_e = 0, hit_e = 10/N and RESULT exactly 0; a randomly relabelled table gives 10/N in expectation and RESULT ~0.0000x, with no sampling needed; a perfectly ranked but oversized cell is penalised by exactly the number of slots it consumes, which is exactly the recall it costs. Over Q_H and HBAA it adds the whole ranked negative list instead of a mean over ten negatives, plus cell occupancy, plus the hard 10-slot budget that is the actual evaluation boundary; over expected rank it adds truncation and slot arithmetic, so being ranked third inside a 500-item cell no longer looks good. It is not a margin, tightness, likelihood or coverage functional, and it does not live on the single-anchor contrast.
metrics.compute: one O(N) pass to build the cell index and the counts n_c; m <= 256 cell barycentres costing O(N) in total; then per training example one barycentre over |H_e| points and one distance vector of length m <= 256. At ~1e5 examples and 256 cells this is 2.6e7 distance evaluations, vectorised over examples in blocks of 4096, i.e. a few seconds in numpy and well under 15 s end to end; memory O(N*d). If the training split exceeds 1e5 examples, take every ceil(n_e / 1e5)-th example (a fixed compute cap, not a fitted parameter).
metrics.risks: the uniform-within-cell assumption is the main exposure: if Stage 3 orders items inside a cell better than uniform the number under-rates coarse tables, and if worse it over-rates them. The query is the reference history barycentre, so a table that suits a different Stage-3 query encoder is mispredicted. The [0,1] clamp and the 10/N subtraction compress the upper range, which can cost Spearman resolution if many of the 97 tables sit near the ceiling. A strongly unbalanced level-1 partition makes the average dominated by the few small cells, so part of the signal could be balance rather than geometry; the chance subtraction removes only the target-independent part. Curvature may turn out to matter little, as hbaa_euclid (+0.693 at curvature 1e-3) suggests, in which case the number is carried by the ranking and occupancy, though the construction remains hyperbolic. Levels 2..L are deliberately unused, so a table that is good only below level 1 is scored as flat.
metrics.failure_mode: it must be worst on the one-code table, all 24587 items in a single level-1 cell: every target sits behind zero cells, hit_e = 10/N for every example, and RESULT is exactly 0. Second worst on the lumped table that spends all 255 remaining codes on singletons and puts the other 24332 items in the last cell: the target is almost always in the lump, hit_e = 10/24332, RESULT ~1e-4, even though the 255 singleton cells rank perfectly. It is also near 0 on any table whose level-1 code is a bijective relabelling of the item id for the first 256 items with the tail lumped, because nothing at cell granularity is rankable.

metrics.title: Cross-view Gromov common-ancestor AUC of the level-1 SID cells against the full training history, lifted to zero by size-weighted negatives.
metrics.inputs: the exported SID table (integer code per item at level 1); the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference source/target representation arrays s_v and t_v; the TRAINING split pairs P. Nothing else.
metrics.geometry: Curvature K=-1 enters three times and is not removable. (1) d is the Poincare metric of a ball of fixed negative curvature, so (x|y)_o is a Gromov product; by construction it is the depth of the lowest common ancestor in the reference's tree-like semantic hierarchy, i.e. "the cell lies in the same semantic subtree as the query". (2) q_i and c_h are geodesic (Lorentz/Frechet) barycentres, minimisers of summed squared geodesic distance on the hyperboloid, not Euclidean means. (3) the comparison of A_i(h) with A_i(h(i)) is a tangent-space/common-ancestor comparison that is only defined because both points were lifted through the exponential map into the same negatively curved ball; a Euclidean distance on raw codes or raw features has neither the common-ancestor reading nor the exponential volume growth.
metrics.why: Stage 3 recalls i iff the generator, conditioned on the query, emits i's SID in the top 10. That requires (a) i's first code to be the code the query's semantics predict, and (b) that code to outrank the competing codes. HG measures (a) and (b): q_i aggregates the WHOLE training history of i (all co-occurring source items), not one anchor and not a mean of ten negatives; c_h is built on the TARGET head, the side the generator must hit; and the statistic is taken against the ENTIRE size-weighted negative code distribution, so a cell is rewarded only if it beats most competing cells rather than the mean of ten convenient negatives. Adds over Q_H: Q_H scores the prefix ordering of items by their own reference geometry and never asks whether the code is the one the query predicts, so it cannot separate a semantically coherent code from a merely tidy one. Adds over HBAA: HBAA is a single signed margin (u_h|mu_+) - (u_h|mu_-) against one positive barycentre and one mean-over-ten-negative barycentre, on the source head; HG replaces that mean by the full negative distribution as a rank/AUC, making it invariant to the scale and offset of the Gromov products and ungameable by a few easy negatives, and it uses the target head for the codebook, i.e. the actual retrieval direction. The AUC form gives the right degeneracy: a one-code table has E_i=1/2 for every i (HG=0) and a random relabelling is exchangeable so E[1{A_i(h)<A_i(h(i))}]=1/2 (HG~0), so collapse is never rewarded.
metrics.compute: Lorentz lifts plus |I| history barycentres and K1 cell barycentres are closed form: O(N*d) time and O(N*d) memory (d<=256, N=24587, K1<=256). The alignment stage is |I|*K1 Gromov products, each three Poincare distances of O(d), i.e. at most 24587*256 ~ 6.3e6 products (~1.6e9 multiply-adds), fully vectorisable in numpy, a few seconds. Whole metric well under one minute.
metrics.risks: (i) the Gromov product carries a radial depth term, so cells whose centroid sits near the boundary can look aligned with every query; size weighting and the 1/2 same-cell credit reduce but do not remove this. (ii) if the source and target heads are not in a common ball/curvature the cross-view product is ill-defined; it must be the shared B^d_{-1} exported by Issue #126, else the statistic degenerates to noise. (iii) sparse training pairs make |H(i)| and |I| small, so the estimate is noisy. (iv) points near ||x||=1 make arcosh overflow; clamp ||x|| <= 1-1e-6 in double precision. (v) tiny K1 makes the AUC coarse and can leave it near 0 for every table.
metrics.failure_mode: the worst table is the adversarial anti-alignment that assigns every item i the level-1 code whose Gromov alignment with q_i is SMALLEST (the exact reverse of the metric's preference), driving HG to about -(1/2)*(N-K1)/(N-1), the minimum. The degenerate one-code table (K1=1) is the worst structured case: there is no h != h(i), so E_i=1/2 for all i and HG=0 exactly by construction, and a uniformly random relabelling also gives HG~0, so neither collapse nor noise is rewarded. The metric is also near 0 when the target head is uninformative relative to the source head, because then all A_i(h) are nearly equal.

metrics.title: Hyperbolic Gromov-ancestry AUC of the level-1 cell (two-tree agreement between the trie's branch and the reference's common-ancestor depth)
metrics.formula:
Items i=1..N (N=24587), integer codes k_i=(k_i1,...,k_iL). Reference points x_s(i), x_t(i) in the Poincare ball B_c={p in R^d : c||p||^2<1} of curvature -c, with c=c_R (the curvature stored with the frozen reference artifact; no new constant).
  d(u,v) = (1/sqrt(c)) * arcosh( 1 + 2c||u-v||^2 / ((1-c||u||^2)(1-c||v||^2)) ).
  For every training interaction (u,i) used as a query: target i+=i, history H(u,i) = the training items of u strictly before i, truncated to the most recent 200 (compute cap, not tuned).
  Query point q = Einstein midpoint of {x_s(j) : j in H}: k_j = 2x_s(j)/(1+c||x_s(j)||^2) (Klein), g_j = 1/sqrt(1-c||k_j||^2), s = sum_j (1/|H|) g_j k_j, k_q = s/||s||, q = k_q/(1+sqrt(1-c||k_q||^2)).
  r_q = d(q,o), r_j = d(x_t(j),o) with o=0 (ball centre).
  G_j = 0.5*( r_q + r_j - d(q, x_t(j)) )  ==  the Gromov product (q|x_t(j))_o in (B_c,d).
  S+ = { j != i+ : k_j1 == k_{i+}1 },  S- = { j != i+ : k_j1 != k_{i+}1 }, n+=|S+|, n-=|S-|.
  AUC_u = [ sum_{j in S+} rank_{S+ U S-}(G_j) - n+(n++1)/2 ] / (n+ * n-), ranks with mid-ranks for ties.
  HGCA = (1/|Q|) * sum_{u in Q} ( 2*AUC_u - 1 ).  A query with n+=0 or n-=0 contributes exactly 0. Range [-1,+1], higher better. Q = all training interactions; if |Q|>4096, take every ceil(|Q|/4096)-th in fixed order (compute cap).
metrics.inputs: the exported SID table (one integer code per item per level); the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference (x_s(i), x_t(i) per item, its curvature c_R, training-pairs-only); the TRAINING split (user, item, order) to form histories. Nothing else.
metrics.geometry: curvature is -c_R and enters twice, inseparably. (1) q is a Frechet/Einstein barycentre in the ball; (2) the score is the Gromov product (q|x_j)_o, the depth of the common ancestor of the query and item j in the ball's tree-like structure, with Poincare geodesic lengths. At c->0 the Gromov product degenerates to the flat inner product <q,x_j>, loses all ancestor meaning, and the metric stops comparing two trees. No log map, no tangent vector, no extra curvature constant; the only scale is the reference's own c_R, and AUC is invariant to any monotone rescaling of G.
metrics.why: a Stage-3 Recall@10 miss happens when the target's level-1 branch is not the branch the decoder scores highly for the query, or when that branch drags in too many co-scored competitors. The reference embedding is tree-like: (q|x_j)_o is literally how deep the query's ancestry is shared with item j, and the trie's level-1 code is the code's own claim about that ancestor. HGCA asks, per query, whether the positive's cell holds the items that sit deeper in the query's ancestry than the corpus at large (AUC over all 24587 items), averaged over queries. That is the quantity the prefix beam is trying to rank. Over Q_H it adds: (a) the whole negative distribution through a rank statistic instead of one anchor's prefix rank; (b) like-for-like comparison (ancestor depth vs prefix, not prefix vs raw proximity); (c) the whole training history as the query point (barycentre), not a single anchor; (d) an exact zero under code/geometry independence, so collapse and relabelling are never rewarded and bucket count does not enter the number.
metrics.compute: precompute r_j and c-norms once (O(N d)). Per query: one N x d matrix-vector product for <q,x_t(j)>, the closed-form Poincare distance (O(N d)), then one argsort of N doubles for mid-ranks and a prefix-count pass over the 256 level-1 codes (O(N log N)). 4096 queries x 24587 items is about 10^8 flops and ~4096 sorts, roughly 10-20 s single core, O(N) memory. Fits the one-minute budget.
metrics.risks: G_j is bounded by min(r_q,r_j), so for co-radial items it is largely a radius/frequency term and the metric may partly be a popularity detector, over-crediting tables that reproduce frequency. Long histories collapse q toward the origin (small r_q), degrading G to 0.5*r_j and amplifying that confound. Level-1 only: two tables with the same level-1 partition but different deeper levels score identically (deliberate, since level >=2 is item-ID-like). Tables with extreme bucket counts give few contributing queries and a noisier average. If the stored reference points are in a differently normalised ball than c_R implies, G is distorted.
metrics.failure_mode: worst on a level-1 code anti-aligned with the reference's ancestry, e.g. codes assigned by the angular sector opposite to each item's reference position, so the positive's cell holds exactly the items sharing least ancestry with the query: every AUC_u < 0.5 and HGCA goes to -1. It is exactly 0 on the tables that should be neutral: a one-code table (S- empty, every query contributes 0) and a randomly relabelled or round-robin-over-id table (codes independent of geometry, AUC=0.5).

metrics.title: Size-matched, decoder-temperatured hyperbolic predictive-mass lift of each item's level-1 SID cell, queried by its full training-history Frechet barycentre.
metrics.formula: Let B = {x in R^d : c||x||^2 < 1} be the Poincare ball of curvature -c, c > 0, with c the frozen Issue #126 reference's curvature (if it is not exported, c = 1). Mobius addition: x (+) y = ((1 + 2c<x,y> + c||y||^2)x + (1 - c||x||^2)y) / (1 + 2c<x,y> + c^2||x||^2||y||^2). exp_x(v) = x (+) (tanh(sqrt(c)||v||/2) v / (sqrt(c)||v||)); log_x(y) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||) ((-x)(+)y) / ||(-x)(+)y||; d_B(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) arcosh(1 + 2c||x-y||^2 / ((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2))). For a finite set S in B, mu(S) = argmin_{x in B} sum_{s in S} d_B(x,s)^2, computed from x_0 = the radius-clipped Euclidean mean by 20 iterations of x <- exp_x( (1/|S|) sum_{s in S} log_x(s) ) (a Frechet/Karcher barycentre). For item i: a_i is its frozen reference SOURCE representation, b_i its frozen reference TARGET representation, both projected into B by scaling to radius at most (1/sqrt(c))(1 - 1e-5). H_i = the items of i's user that occur strictly before i in the training split's fixed order, excluding i. u_i = mu({a_k : k in H_i}). tau = the frozen reference's own softmax temperature (its logit scale); if not exported, tau = 1/sqrt(c). p_i(k) = exp(-d_B(u_i,b_k)/tau) / sum_{m=1..N} exp(-d_B(u_i,b_m)/tau), evaluated by log-sum-exp. L1(i) = the level-1 integer code of item i; cell(i) = {k : L1(k) = L1(i)}; s_i = |cell(i)|; N = the number of items in the table. P_i = sum_{k in cell(i)} p_i(k). Q is the deterministic set of M = 2*256 = 512 query items: keep training items with |H_i| >= 1, sort them by integer item id, and for t = 0..M-1 take the item at index floor(t*(n-1)/(M-1)) (or all n if n < M); Q depends only on the training split and the codebook size 256, never on the SID table or on any recall. METRIC = (N/M) * sum_{i in Q} P_i/s_i - 1. One scalar, higher is better. No constant is fitted to the 97 recalls: c and tau come from the reference, M = 2*256 from the codebook size, 20 and 1e-5 are convergence and float-projection constants, N from the table.
metrics.inputs: the exported SID table (integer code per item and level; level 1 is used); the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference's per-item source array a and target array b, plus its curvature c and temperature tau; the TRAINING split (user-item interactions in their fixed order) to build H_i. Nothing else: no validation interaction, no test interaction, no recall, no Stage-3 output.
metrics.geometry: the query point is a Karcher/Frechet barycentre in the curvature -c ball, built with the Poincare exp and log maps and Mobius addition, so it is not a Euclidean mean; the score is the Poincare geodesic distance d_B; the normaliser is a softmax over geodesic distances at the reference's own temperature. Curvature enters in d_B's denominator (1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2), in every exp/log of the barycentre iteration, and in the temperature fallback 1/sqrt(c). The c -> 0 limit is a Euclidean mean and a Euclidean softmax and a numerically different number, so this is not a Euclidean distance in disguise.
metrics.why: Stage 3 visits a level-1 cell only if the reference's own decoder assigns that cell enough probability mass for the query, so the quantity governing Recall@10 is exactly P_i, the temperatured predictive mass the decoder places on the item's cell. Dividing by the closed-form null s_i/N, the expected mass of a uniformly random size-matched cell (each item lies in the cell with probability s_i/N and the softmax sums to 1), makes the number a lift over chance: the factor by which the table's cell beats a random cell of the same size. It adds three things over HBAA, which estimates the same log-likelihood ratio from one positive and the mean of ten sampled negatives: (i) the full negative distribution with the decoder's exponential weights, hence no ten-negative sampling variance; (ii) a closed-form size-matched null, so a 1-code table scores exactly 0 and a random relabel scores ~0, and neither large nor collapsed cells are rewarded; (iii) the whole training history as the query point (the barycentre of its items' source representations) rather than a single anchor. It is not an expected rank either: it keeps the magnitude of the probability gap, which is what the beam consumes, not only the order. It is not a coverage, margin, tightness, adjacency-R2 or path-likelihood statistic, all of which were measured and failed.
metrics.compute: M = 512 queries times N = 24587 targets = 1.26e7 Poincare distances of dimension d (about 8e8 flops at d = 64), evaluated in query chunks so memory stays bounded; plus 512 Karcher means over histories of average length about 10 at 20 iterations each, and two log-sum-exp passes per query. Vectorised NumPy: a few seconds, comfortably under one minute on 24587 items and 256 codes.
metrics.risks: (a) tau matters: if the reference temperature is very small the softmax collapses to a 1-nearest-neighbour indicator and the metric becomes a noisy cell hit-rate; if it is very large P_i -> s_i/N and the metric flattens to 0 for every table. tau is used verbatim because Stage 3 uses the same value, so the risk is inherited rather than introduced. (b) Global popularity is not controlled: a table that groups globally popular items can raise P_i without personalisation, since the null controls cell size but not item frequency. (c) Level-1 only: at most 256 cells, so two tables with the same level-1 partition but different deeper branches get identical scores; if Stage-3 recall is driven by deeper branching the metric is blind to it. (d) If the reference representations are nearly Euclidean the curvature term contributes little and the value approaches its c -> 0 limit. (e) Items with empty or one-item histories are excluded from Q, and the 512-query sample adds sampling noise. (f) If the training split's temporal order is not fixed and reproducible, H_i is ill-defined.
metrics.failure_mode: the table on which it must be worst is the anti-coherent derangement: a valid 256-code level-1 partition whose cells are built so that each item shares its cell with the items the reference finds LEAST probable given that item's history (for example, assign codes in reverse order of the items' frequency-sorted predictive rank, so every cell is a set of mutually unpredictable items). There P_i << s_i/N for almost every query and the metric is strongly negative, because it is a lift with no floor at 0. The one-code table gives exactly 0 (P_i = 1, s_i = N) and a uniformly random relabelling of any table gives 0 in expectation (E[P_i] = s_i/N), so the ordering is anti-coherent < collapse = random < coherent. A subtler failure is a table that is optimal at level 1 but random below it: it scores as high as the good table, which is a sensitivity failure rather than a low score.
